# tritonctl meta

Project and instance metadata

Subcommands: list, get, set, unset, realized

Usage: `tritonctl meta [OPTIONS] <COMMAND>`

## tritonctl meta list

List every metadata entry at one scope

Alias: ls

Usage: `tritonctl meta list [OPTIONS] --scope <SCOPE>`

- `--scope <SCOPE>` (required; one of: tenant, project, instance)
- `--id <ID>`: The entity at that scope: an instance (name, uuid, or prefix), a project (name, uuid, or prefix; defaults to --project), or a tenant uuid (defaults to yours)

## tritonctl meta get

Read one metadata entry by key

Usage: `tritonctl meta get [OPTIONS] --scope <SCOPE> --key <KEY>`

- `--scope <SCOPE>` (required; one of: tenant, project, instance)
- `--id <ID>`: The entity at that scope: an instance (name, uuid, or prefix), a project (name, uuid, or prefix; defaults to --project), or a tenant uuid (defaults to yours)
- `--key <KEY>`: Metadata key, e.g. `config/ntp-servers`, `guest/leader`, `user-data`. Slash-separated (required)

## tritonctl meta set

Upsert one metadata entry

Usage: `tritonctl meta set [OPTIONS] --scope <SCOPE> --key <KEY> --value <VALUE>`

- `--scope <SCOPE>` (required; one of: tenant, project, instance)
- `--id <ID>`: The entity at that scope: an instance (name, uuid, or prefix), a project (name, uuid, or prefix; defaults to --project), or a tenant uuid (defaults to yours)
- `--key <KEY>` (required)
- `--value <VALUE>`: Value as a JSON literal (e.g. `'"10.0.0.2"'`, `'42'`, `'{"a":1}'`). A bare string without quotes is accepted and stored as a JSON string (required)
- `--guest-visible <GUEST_VISIBLE>`: Override the default guest-visibility for this key (one of: true, false)
- `--guest-writable`: Mark this key guest-writable. Only meaningful on `guest/*` keys at instance scope; the server rejects it elsewhere

## tritonctl meta unset

Delete one metadata entry

Usage: `tritonctl meta unset [OPTIONS] --scope <SCOPE> --key <KEY>`

- `--scope <SCOPE>` (required; one of: tenant, project, instance)
- `--id <ID>`: The entity at that scope: an instance (name, uuid, or prefix), a project (name, uuid, or prefix; defaults to --project), or a tenant uuid (defaults to yours)
- `--key <KEY>` (required)
- `-n, --dry-run`: Print what would change and stop
- `-y, --yes`: Answer yes to the confirmation. The summary still prints
- `--keep-going`: Keep executing after a step fails

## tritonctl meta realized

The full realized view for one instance: the precedence merge of project/instance metadata plus the computed system keys, each leaf tagged with the scope it came from

Usage: `tritonctl meta realized [OPTIONS] --instance <INSTANCE>`

- `--instance <INSTANCE>`: Instance name, uuid, or prefix (required)
